land.text: Acarnania, which after Actium in 31 BCE became part of the Roman province of Achaea; Augustus removed the inhabitants of several towns to Nicopolis

successors.note: The Roman Empire row starts 31 BCE in Cliopatria (roman-republic ends 32).

capitals.name: Stratos
capitals.note: The League's assembly 'met at Stratos' (League page) and 'The capital and principal city in ancient times was Stratos' (Acarnania page). Coordinates are the researcher's approximation of the site near Agrinio; neither page gives them.

capitals.name: Leucas
capitals.note: In the 230 BCE reconstitution, 'Leucas was its capital' (League page). Approximate coordinates of Lefkada town.

capitals.name: Thyrreion
capitals.note: After Pydna Rome 'separated' Leucas and 'the city of Thyrreion was appointed the new capital' (Acarnania page). Approximate coordinates; the site is not in the gazetteer.

correction.text: Acarnania: the Ionian coast from the Ambracian Gulf to the Achelous, with Leucas, under the federal League of Stratos

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Acarnanian League; checked with the gazetteer on 2026-10-19, a 50 km disc round Acarnania (centre 21.0 E 38.7 N) falls in Macedonian Empire (11 cells) and Greek City-States (10) in 310, the Aetolian League (8) in 230, Greek City-States (3) with the Aetolian League (8) in 200, Greek City-States (11) in 150 and the Roman Republic (11) in 100 and 60. The Acarnania page gives about 4,070 km2 and bounds it by the Ambracian Gulf, the Ionian Sea and the Achelous. The League page says it 'existed since the 5th century BC'; this dossier starts at Cassander's federal reorganisation of 314 BCE, the first dated step in the pages opened (the 5th-century and 4th-century phases, the 375/4 entry into the Second Athenian League and the 390 Spartan alliance, belong to the Greece group before Alexander's death).

correction.text: the reconstituted League of 230 BCE, of which 'only Anaktorion, Palairos, Thyrreion, and Medion were members', with Leucas as capital: the north and west of Acarnania, without the southern part held by Aetolia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: no territory is drawn for 249-231 because the League page records the partition of c. 250 and a reconstitution in 230, and neither page says the League held any land in between. The southern disc (centre 21.1 E 38.55 N, 38 km: Stratos, Agrinio and Oeniadae) is the researcher's cut for the Aetolian share; the pages give only 'the Acheloos River as their mutual border' and the south 'incorporated into the Aetolian League'. [Reviewer eu-02-x, 2026-10-19: 'to' moved from -169 to -190 because ledger 4 returns the southern part in 189; the new keyframe acarnanian-league_-189 carries 189-169]

correction.text: Acarnania to the Achelous with Leucas: the League of Leucas with the southern part back, 'Under the Romans, or probably a little earlier, the river Achelous formed the boundary between Acarnania and Aetolia'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe added by the reviewer (eu-02-x, 2026-10-19) so the shapes agree with ledger 4 (the c. 189 return of the south, a confidence-1 bridge from the aetolian-league dossier, not the page). Leucas stays in until 168, when it 'was separated from Acarnania' (Acarnania page).

correction.text: Acarnania to the Achelous without Leucas, which 'was separated from Acarnania' by Rome in 168 BCE

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from 168 the shape is Acarnania less Leucas. That the southern part is back under the League by then is a bridge (confidence 1): the Acarnania page says only that under the Romans or a little earlier the Achelous formed the boundary with Aetolia.

ledger.note: 314: Cassander reorganises the Acarnanian League 'on a truly federal basis'. Acarnania page: settlements near the Aetolian frontier were merged into fewer, larger ones 'at the behest of the Macedonian king Cassander'. The League itself 'existed since the 5th century BC'; this is the first dated step.

region.text: the southern part of Acarnania (Stratos, Oeniadae) taken into the Aetolian League

ledger.note: c. 250: Acarnania is partitioned. 'partitioned between Aetolia and Epirus in, c. 250 BC'; the League page has the Acarnanians and Aetolians make peace 'in ca. 270 BCE' after Pyrrhus's death and agree 'the Acheloos River as their mutual border', the south 'incorporated into the Aetolian League'. The two pages differ by twenty years; 250 follows the Acarnania page and the aetolian-league dossier.

region.text: the northern part of Acarnania with Leucas, to Epirus

ledger.note: c. 250 (or ca. 270): 'the northern part with Leucas went to Epirus' (League page); Acarnania page: 'partitioned between Aetolia and Epirus in, c. 250 BC'.

region.text: the north and west of Acarnania with Leucas

ledger.note: 230: the League is reconstituted. In the 230 BCE reconstitution, 'Leucas was its capital' and 'only Anaktorion, Palairos, Thyrreion, and Medion were members'. Epirus page: western Acarnania 'asserted its independence' in the c. 233 account that ends the Epirote kingdom (infobox 231). The land is the researcher's reading of the member cities.

region.text: the southern part of Acarnania back from Aetolia

ledger.note: c. 189 (bridge): the southern part returns. The Acarnania page says only that 'the river Achelous formed the boundary between Acarnania and Aetolia' under the Romans or a little earlier; no page opened dates the Aetolian loss of Stratos and Oeniadae. 189 is the Roman reduction of the Aetolian League on the aetolian-league dossier.
168: after Pydna Rome takes Leucas from the League. 'Leucas was separated from Acarnania' and 'the city of Thyrreion was appointed the new capital'.

region.text: Acarnania, now under the province of Achaea and Nicopolis

ledger.note: 31 BCE: the League ends. 'It was only after the Battle of Actium in 31 BCE' that the League became part of the Roman province of Achaea; the Acarnania page: 'The inhabitants of several of its towns were removed by Augustus to Nicopolis' and 'Acarnania fell under that city's rule'.

wars.name: Second Macedonian War
wars.outcome: The Acarnanians were 'forced to capitulate to the Roman Republic'.
wars.note: The page gives the war's span, not the year of the capitulation or the side the Acarnanians took.

wars.name: Roman-Seleucid War

zones.text: Acarnania, invaded by Antiochus III in 191

wars.outcome: The Acarnanians 'were persuaded by their countryman Mnasilochus to espouse' Antiochus's cause in 191; no loss of land is on the page.
wars.note: The Acarnania page dates only Antiochus III's invasion of Greece (191 BC) and gives no span for the war, so only 191 is recorded.

certainty.note: Only the Achelous is named as a frontier (with Aetolia, ca. 270 per the League page); the Epirote and Aetolian cuts of 250 and the Leucas cut of 168 are the researcher's discs.

notes: Three pages. No Cliopatria row; everything is a new keyframe. 'Acarnania' is not in the gazetteer (a region name for the gazetteer agent: the Ionian coast of Greece between the Ambracian Gulf and the Achelous, with Leucas, roughly 20.6-21.3 E, 38.3-39.0 N); the southern share (Stratos, Oeniadae) and Leucas are discs, the researcher's cuts, not the pages' lines. The pages disagree on the partition: ca. 270 BCE after Pyrrhus's death (League page) against c. 250 (Acarnania page and aetolian-league's dossier); on Leucas (League page: it went to Epirus; Acarnania page: Leucas became the regional capital after the Epirote king fell, c. 300-250); the reconstitution 230 (League page) against c. 233 (Epirus page). The League has no territory 249-231 in this dossier (a dormant state). Not on any page: the year of the capitulation to Rome in the Second Macedonian War, the Aetolian seizure of Oeniadae in 211 (antigonid-dynasty and aetolian-league carry it), the 189 settlement (the return of the south is a bridge). Mirrors needed: aetolian-league has the c. 250 gain from 'Acarnanian League' (now a slug that exists); kingdom-of-epirus needs a c. 250 gain of north Acarnania and Leucas and a 230 loss; roman-republic needs a 168 gain of Leucas (part of its 167 Epirus gain?). Earlier life (5th century to 314) and Nicopolis are outside this batch.
